lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Hi Daniel, thanks for making the time. Before we start — this call is being recorded for note-taking, is that okay with you?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yeah, that's fine.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Great. So when we spoke briefly at the expo you mentioned your team spends a lot of time writing up customer calls. Can you walk me through how that works today?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Sure. We've got eleven account managers, and after every customer call they're supposed to log notes in the CRM. In practice maybe half of it gets logged, and what does get logged is inconsistent.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: When you say inconsistent — what's the actual cost of that for you?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Two things. Handovers are painful — when an AM leaves or is out, whoever picks up the account is flying blind. And my QBR prep takes me a full day because I'm chasing people for what actually happened on their accounts.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Got it. And is fixing this something you're actively looking at this quarter, or more of a background annoyance?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: It's active. My COO flagged call documentation in our ops review in June. I've been asked to bring a proposal to the leadership meeting in September.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Okay, that's useful. Who besides you and the COO would weigh in on a decision like this?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: IT security would need to review anything that touches customer data. And finance signs off on anything over ten thousand a year.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Is ten thousand roughly the zone you'd expect a tool like this to land in, or do you have a number in mind?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Honestly I budgeted around fifteen thousand a year for this in the proposal draft. If it's meaningfully above that it gets harder.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That's workable. Let me show you how the call notes look — every claim in the summary links back to the exact line in the transcript, so your AMs can verify before anything goes to the CRM.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That's actually important. We had a bad experience with an AI notetaker that made things up. One wrong number in a customer note caused a real mess with a client last year.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That's exactly the problem we built around — if there's no supporting line in the transcript, the claim doesn't ship. It gets dropped and flagged instead.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Okay. My main concern after that is security review. Customer call recordings are sensitive — where does the audio live, and who can see it?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Fair question. I'll send you our security overview and data retention docs today so IT can start early. Recordings are deletable on demand and we can walk your team through the architecture.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Send that over. If security is comfortable, I'd want to pilot with three AMs before September.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Let's do that. So next steps: I send the security docs today, we set up a pilot with three of your AMs in August, and I'll put together pricing that fits the fifteen thousand envelope. Can we book thirty minutes next Thursday to review the pilot plan?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thursday works. Morning if possible.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Thursday morning it is. Thanks Daniel — you'll have the docs in your inbox this afternoon.

follow_up_email.subject: Security docs + Thursday pilot review — Open Gong x Brightline
follow_up_email.body:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for the conversation today. As promised, I've attached our security overview and data-retention documentation so your IT team can start their review early.

Recapping what we agreed:
- Pilot with three of your AMs in August, pending IT security sign-off
- Pricing scoped to fit the ~$15k/year envelope you've drafted
- 30 minutes Thursday morning to walk through the pilot plan — invite to follow

One thing that stuck with me: your experience with a notetaker that invented details. That's the exact failure mode we designed against — every claim in our notes links to the specific line in the transcript, and anything without proof gets dropped, not shipped.

Talk Thursday,
Maya

fields.name: discovery_quality
fields.justification: Maya quantified the pain (handover blindness, full-day QBR prep), established urgency (COO mandate, September deadline), surfaced the full buying committee, and anchored budget — all with open questions rather than pitching.

fields.name: objection_handling
fields.justification: The accuracy objection was answered directly with the product's evidence gate. The security objection was acknowledged with a concrete same-day action, though no security specifics were given on the call itself.
